_comment: Curated gender for the cast_hints no source tier can reach.
Each of the 14 vendored Folger scenes ships a provenance sidecar carrying a
characters list. Thirty of the 42 shipped cast_hints resolve to male|female
straight off that roster. The remaining twelve do not, for three different
reasons: the speech prefix is absent from the printed dramatis personae
(TOBY, ROBIN), the roster entry exists but the fetched text never gendered it
(HELENA, HERMIA, LYSANDER, DEMETRIUS carry a populated roster_name and an
empty description), or the prefix is a shared family name that two source
people answer to (ANTIPHOLUS and DROMIO are each two brothers, both recorded
gender='unknown').
The alternative was an address-form heuristic over the whole play text. That
text is not on disk -- the 14 vendored files are SLICED SCENES, and the
vendor rebinds body to the slice one line after parsing the roster -- so the
heuristic would need a network re-vendor to run at all, and it still reaches
neither ANTIPHOLUS nor DON PEDRO. Ten committed lines are offline,
deterministic, reviewable as a data diff, and survive a re-vendor, because
the vendor rewrites sidecars and never this file.
ARIEL and PUCK are deliberately NOT here. Folger's stage directions use 'he'
for both, but neither has a defensible roster fact and both are genuinely
editorial calls that belong to the operator. They stay on the existing roll,
which is why the corpus test asserts 40 of 42 rather than 42 of 42.
MERGE RULE, enforced in _otr_roster_gender.load_gender_supplement and
resolve_with_supplement: an entry may only fill a slot the roster left
unknown, every entry must carry a non-empty evidence string, and an entry
that contradicts a CONFIRMED sidecar gender raises rather than winning.

ANTIPHOLUS.evidence: Both Antipholus twins are sons of Egeon and Emilia; the sidecar records ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS and ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE with gender_source=unknown, so the shared speech prefix cannot be joined, but neither brother is a woman.

DROMIO.evidence: Both Dromio twins are the bondmen attending the Antipholus twins; the sidecar records DROMIO OF EPHESUS and DROMIO OF SYRACUSE as gender='unknown', so the shared prefix abstains at the join.

LUCE.evidence: Folger dramatis personae: Luce (also called Nell), kitchen maid to Adriana; Dromio of Syracuse calls her 'the kitchen wench'

BALTHASAR.evidence: Folger dramatis personae: Balthasar, a merchant; Antipholus of Ephesus addresses him as 'good Signior Balthasar'

BOTTOM.evidence: Nick Bottom the weaver, one of the Athenian mechanicals; addressed throughout as a man and cast as Pyramus in their play.

LYSANDER.evidence: One of the two Athenian young men in love with Hermia; the sidecar carries roster_name='LYSANDER' with an empty description, so the fetched Folger text simply never gendered the entry.

DEMETRIUS.evidence: The other Athenian suitor, whom Egeus prefers for Hermia; sidecar carries roster_name='DEMETRIUS' with an empty description.

HELENA.evidence: In love with Demetrius and Hermia's childhood friend; sidecar carries roster_name='HELENA' with an empty description.

HERMIA.evidence: Egeus's daughter, in love with Lysander; sidecar carries roster_name='HERMIA' with an empty description.

TOBY.evidence: Sir Toby Belch, Olivia's kinsman; the manifest hint drops the honorific so the prefix TOBY is recorded absent_from_roster with an empty roster_name.

DON PEDRO.evidence: Don Pedro, Prince of Aragon; the sidecar's PRINCE entry is gender='unknown', so neither the hint nor a rename reaches a gendered roster fact.

HORATIO.evidence: Hamlet's fellow scholar and confidant at Elsinore; the sidecar entry carries no gendered description.
